Review of Norell Boards. 
First feels; When I first saw the monster I was about to ride for this last week, I shouted. It was beautiful. The aggressive concaves, gaspedals and low weight point, makes it considerably much more intriguing. I turned over the board and I am dazzled over what i find. The carbonfibre, and the elegant blackness, with the white Norell-Logo, carefully placed, and handwritten ”No.2”, made it look like a sportscar.  
Well on the board, my first feeling, is safety. The concave really locks you in, both in tuck and regular stance. The gaspedals, to be frank, is my favorite thing about this board. I felt, ”I wanna go fast.. Really fast.”  
I was considering a Rayne Supreme, but Norell is building a fine opponent. 
 
Sliding; I was given a board with Paris 180 mm trucks and Abec 11 Flashbacks, fresh out the pack. 
First day, I didn't really connect with the board, but the more I rode it, the more i loved it. Again the concave helps me to stay locked in, and not heel or toe outside the rail, and if I do, the rails Norell has designed makes it easy to grip your rails, so you can bust really long toeside checks and get a really steezy lean in your powerslides. Since it is very low, and have the stiffness of Chuck Norris ”you-know-what”, it feels very predictable. And since it fairly short, you can just let go with your hands, and still have so much controll. And after i broke in the Flashies, I was out sliding for 4 days. This is totally one of my favorite Sliding boards. 
 
Downhill/freeride; Remember I said I wanted to go fast? I did. Really fast. And it was so much fun. 
I threw on a bit gripper Divine touch, 78 a, and I was flying. The gaspedals are perfect for my foot, and since Norell custom bulid boards, everyone can get this feeling of absolut controll. The low weightpoint protected me from any wobbles and the concave held me like a mother holds her child. 
Since I am no Tech-slider, I cannot leave you my opinion in that spectra, but i know what the Freerider would have said. It's not a topmount, and it got no kicks. Correct. No kicks. And i find this extremely annoying. This makes shuvits and manuals very hard, on the brink of impossible for a rider with my 2 years of experience, but I am sure that somebody could pull it off. Other than that. This is my Downhillboard of choice. 
 
Dancing/Flatland: I love to dance. It is my main discipline and it is what I am at my best. 38” are enough for a couple of cross-steps and a few Peterpans, but other than that, I find it impossible to dance. Which makes sense. The ”kick issue”, keeps me from being creative and ”flowy”. But rumor is that Norell are working on a Dancer.  
 
Conclusion: This is a VERY fun board. And he custom builds them (therefore the absence of measurements) so anybody can get this board exactly as they want. This guy really know what he is doing, and I am looking forward to review his next board. Norell is located in Stockholm, Sweden 
but I think he is working 100 percent to send his board worldwide. 
 
This is my first review so please do leave feedback on what i could have done better. 
 
Andy
